lesson_title: Simple vs Compound: The R98,56 That Appeared From Nowhere
hook_text: Same R5 000. Same 8%. Two answers, R98,56 apart. Where did the extra money come from?
clip_script: Year one: 8 percent of 5 000 is R400, same as before. But here is the move: the R400 does not stand outside — it JOINS the account. You now have R5 400 working for you. Year two: 8 percent of 5 400 — not of 5 000 — which is R432. See the extra R32? That is interest earned by last year's R400. The interest got a job. Balance: R5 832. Year three: 8 percent of 5 832 is R466,56. Balance: R6 298,56. Put the two finals side by side: R6 200 the wage way, R6 298,56 the taxi way. The R98,56 difference is not magic — you just watched it arrive.
visual_style: Stacked coin animation: a fixed R400 stack arriving each year on one side, while on the other side each new stack physically merges into the pile and the next stack grows visibly bigger, with a running counter racing at the top.
pacing: Steady year-by-year beat with the counter accelerating, pause on the R32 reveal, punchy side-by-side finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to master both growth formulas.
